findings.symbol: voice acceptance event observer and completion predicate
findings.problem: Spoken acceptance checks generated transcript plus any non-silent audio sample, then stops the call without tracking successful response completion or drained output playback.
findings.reproduction: Evaluate the exact line-87 waitForFunction predicate with fixture devices=[{name:"test fixture"}], spoken="test fixture", audioPeak=2 and error=null, after transcript.done but before response.done or output_audio_buffer.stopped. It returns true. The next path clicks Stop and emits spoken_grounded_answer PASS.
findings.consequence: Production acceptance may truncate the spoken answer or pass before a later response failure; required spoken completion has not been proved.
findings.fix: Correlate successful grounded transcript, completed response and stopped playback; reject failed/cancelled/cleared responses.
regression_tests: scripts/mcp_spoken_completion.test.mjs: transcript and partial RTP never prove spoken completion

findings.problem: Approval event arguments are discarded; UI shows only tool name. Every execute_device_action approval has the same visible description regardless of device/property/requested state.
findings.reproduction: Feed two mcp_approval_request items with name execute_device_action and different state_key arguments. Actual compiled McpLifecycle returns objects with only id/name; UI displays identical prompts. Locally reproduced using dist/mcp.js.
findings.consequence: User approves an actuator operation without seeing its target or requested change. ID/double-click guards do not establish informed authorization.
findings.fix: Validate bounded approval context against imported schemas and show exact target/property/state without opaque credentials; malformed context blocks approval.
regression_tests: packages/voice-core/tests/mcp.test.mjs: approval context keeps exact target and state and removes opaque credentials

findings.problem: Existing signing-key directory and file are chmodded but neither ownership enforced nor validated. Later chown targets only APP/CONTROL/PUBLIC.
findings.reproduction: Pre-existing SECRET directory and signing.key owned by service UID with modes0700/0600 retain that owner after the exact chmod operations. Local synthetic filesystem repro confirms chmod preserves non-root owner. No production secret accessed.
findings.consequence: Existing misowned authority remains accessible and writable by service user, violating root-only host-managed signing authority; service compromise can mint session/action credentials.
findings.fix: Require root-owned regular non-symlink authority with private directory/file modes before reading; never adopt an exposed key or rotate it during deploy.

findings.problem: Enabled entries with blank, whitespace-only or Ignoruj classification pass validation and are both discoverable and executable.
findings.scenario: Using existing LiveClient fixture, replace lamp policy entry with enabled=true and device_type="", "   ", or "Ignoruj"; search returns count1 and exact off execute returns accepted in all three cases.
findings.consequence: Malformed/inconsistent manual policy can grant access to explicitly ignored or unclassified devices, violating authoritative fail-closed safety.
findings.fix: One classification invariant fails closed across search/state/execute for blank and ignored classifications regardless of enabled flag.

findings.problem: Slug-derived allowed-state keys are not injective; distinct HA effects/options can share identical state_key, so exact tuple cannot identify the requested state.
findings.scenario: Fake light.effect_list=["calm-night","calm night"] yields two allowed states both effect_calm_night. Select the second public state and execute exact tuple; mock HA receives effect="calm-night" (first state), although second displayed label is calm night. Analogous select options differ only punctuation/diacritics/case, or map two raw aliases to same canonical key.
findings.consequence: Approved exact state executes a different HA action payload, defeating the exact device/property/state contract.
findings.fix: Exact raw dynamic choices have deterministic digest-bound unique state keys; ambiguous exact bindings reject.

findings.problem: Device aggregate availability treats HA unknown state as available, while _current_value marks it unavailable.
findings.scenario: _availability([{entity_id:"light.test"}], {"light.test":{state:"unknown"}}) returns available/active. Search availability=available therefore includes a device with only unknown properties.
findings.consequence: Availability filter and spoken grounding can claim a device is available despite no usable current state; mixed unknown/available devices are incorrectly fully available.
findings.fix: Unknown entities are unavailable in aggregate state and filters, consistent with individual properties.

findings.problem: Rollback is not retry-safe when previous canonical source was a directory.
findings.scenario: previous_mcp_directory=true and previous_mcp_path=/opt/home-assistant-mcp; restored directory already exists and backup/previous-mcp-source is absent. This happens before activation moved it, or after a first rollback restored it and failed later at compose/health. Retry executes CANONICAL.symlink_to(previous_mcp_path) over existing directory.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/review-d-repro.py with fake operations: FileExistsError restored_directory_exists=True phase=active
findings.consequence: Persistent watchdog retries stop before restoring legacy unit, Nginx and exact hotel runtime; a transient rollback failure becomes unrecoverable automatically.
findings.fix: Recognize an already restored real directory and safely retry later recovery failures instead of attempting a symlink over it.

findings.symbol: rollback/finalize vs hotel deployment runtime mutations
findings.problem: Rollback is not fenced against concurrent deployment or final acceptance.
findings.scenario: Pause hotel deploy in long-running build. Rollback deadline fires, restores exact images/old routes/backend, marks rolled_back and disables timer. Resume deploy: it unconditionally force-recreates candidate containers and syncs candidate Nginx. Equally, finalize and deadline rollback can both pass their initial active-state check before either changes state.
findings.reproduction: Deterministic interleaving of actual reachable commands: build paused -> rollback docker-compose known-good -> state rolled_back -> hotel line451 candidate up -> line453 candidate nginx reload. No transaction lock, process-group cancellation or phase guard is present in either mutation path.
findings.consequence: Lasting half-cutover: candidate hotel/Nginx with canonical MCP stopped and old backend active, after watchdog protection has been disabled. Concurrent finalize can also delete rollback source while rollback is using it.
findings.fix: Root serialization, revoked transaction state, managed process-group termination and a shared runtime fence prevent late deployment from republishing after rollback.

findings.problem: Private production preflight currently proves only one search, not repeated HA-backed calls or get_device_state.
findings.scenario: A candidate whose HA transport fails after first search passes this preflight; no state request or second search is attempted in the same SDK session.
findings.consequence: The explicit required client-lifetime gate is absent and a previously observed premature-client-close class can reach destructive cutover.
findings.fix: Run search, exact state and repeated search in the same authenticated SDK session; later client failures cannot yield preflight PASS.

findings.title: Final cleanup misses an observed complete legacy verification checkout
findings.scenario: After successful finalize, cleanup removes /opt/home-assistant-agent and /home/ha-agent-deploy/agentha only. The production host also has /home/ha-agent-deploy/smart-verify.Wccqx5 containing app/agent.py and mcp-handler/manifest.json, which is outside all deletion roots.
findings.consequence: Replaced OpenAI agent and MCP handler source/dependencies remain physically installed after claimed final cleanup.
findings.fix: Retire confirmed verification/staging roots after acceptance while preserving canonical source and data.

findings.title: Final cleanup only removes the latest rollback generation and its anchors
findings.scenario: Host has prior rollback directories 20261001T101053207081Z, 20261001T112059339250Z, 20261001T084757Z and 20261001T083834Z with old route/config/env artifacts. Six stopped mcp-rollback hotel anchor containers from the first two generations remain. cleanup loads anchors.json exclusively from state[backup] and deletes only that backup.
findings.consequence: Prior legacy units/routes/env snapshots survive final PASS. Historical anchors can keep replaced hotel images referenced, causing hotel cleanup_accepted_release.py lines 30-34 to skip their deletion.
findings.fix: Retire every coordinator-owned obsolete backup generation and image anchor; prune captured obsolete images only when unused.

A send exception escapes the event handler, leaves microphone/peer active, and consumes the sole followup, so the tool result never reaches a spoken continuation. findings.untested_path: Cleanup command fails after durable accepted phase and rollback timer disabled.
findings.scenario_risk: finalize persists accepted and disables deadline before invoking cleanup. CLI exception handler invokes rollback, which immediately returns for accepted phase. Retrying finalize raises no_active_transaction. Thus a transient docker-rm/cleanup subprocess failure leaves partially retired runtime/backup artifacts with no idempotent finalize retry covered by tests. This is an operational recovery gap, not proof that the accepted runtime is wrong.

Inject each cleanup external failure after one earlier destructive step succeeds, then rerun the supported recovery phase and assert eventual completion, current runtime/source preserved, artifacts removed exactly once, and state accurately exposes accepted-but-cleanup-incomplete until completion.
findings.fix: Persist accepted_cleanup_pending and permit idempotent cleanup retry; never roll back completed acceptance due to retirement failure.

findings.title: Late MCP completion restores interrupted parent grounding after barge-in
findings.repro: Emit response.done(parent,status completed,output [{type:mcp_call,id:call}]); emit input_audio_buffer.speech_started; emit late response.output_item.done(parent,item call search_devices,args {name:recepce},output {status:ok,devices:[synthetic lamp]}); emit response.created(new-user-turn); matching names transcript plus sampled playback and completed/stopped new-user-turn causes ready(devices) true.
findings.impact: The native guide explicitly permits response.done before MCP completion. In that supported ordering, a new user interruption invalidates the pending parent in actual McpLifecycle but not in spoken acceptance: the late old result can falsely ground the next user turn.
findings.partial_fix_verified: Original, pending-parent and cleared-parent false-positive reproductions all now rejected. The remaining late-result-after-barge-in reproduction still returns true.
regression_tests: scripts/mcp_spoken_completion.test.mjs: preexisting unrelated playback cannot borrow successful search grounding
scripts/mcp_spoken_completion.test.mjs: followup requires completed parent and every correlated call terminal
scripts/mcp_spoken_completion.test.mjs: late old MCP completion after barge-in cannot ground a new user turn
findings.resolution_evidence: Independent direct reproductions: original preexisting/cancelled-parent, pending-parent, cleared-parent and response.done-before-late-tool barge-in all false; completed-parent valid follow-up true. Actual browser runtime wire regression old follow-up 0 and new legitimate response.create exactly 1 passed.
findings.fix: Bind semantic successful name-filtered search to its parent or a new follow-up after completed parent/all-call boundary; invalidate interrupted chains and preexisting unrelated responses.

findings.problem: Absolute acceptance deadline is checked only before the potentially blocking final MCP verifier, while finalize holds the transaction lock. Verification may complete after the deadline and still disable rollback and publish acceptance.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/native-final-D-deadline-repro.py executes actual finalize with successful mock runtime/proof/key checks. Clock initially deadline minus one second; final subprocess advances it to deadline plus 120 seconds. finalize completes and publishes accepted. Existing real-process watchdog test establishes the watchdog waits on the same lock.
findings.consequence: A transaction still unaccepted at its configured deadline can evade automatic rollback; stalled verification blocks watchdog beyond its deadline.
findings.regression_test: Clock-crossing successful verifier must never publish accepted/accepted_cleanup_pending or call cleanup; timed-out verifier must release lock and allow watchdog rollback.
findings.resolution_evidence: Actual prior clock-crossing reproduction now raises cutover_acceptance_deadline_expired and retains active phase. Independent real sleeping subprocess was killed and waited on timeout; real watchdog process remained blocked while transaction lock held and performed rollback after lock release.
findings.fix: Bound the final verifier to the remaining rollback deadline and check the deadline again immediately before acceptance commit.

Their current pre-cutover existence is expected and is not an active-runtime defect. Canonical persistent DATA and provenance history must remain preserved.

findings.untested_path: response.created(old) -> input_audio_buffer.speech_started -> first response.mcp_call.in_progress(old) -> response.done(completed,old) -> response.output_item.done(old)
findings.risk: Response.created does not allocate a turn. Barge-in only cancels turns already allocated by an MCP event or response.done. A pre-barge-in response whose first MCP event arrives afterwards is allocated with cancelled=false and emits followup=true after completion; VoiceRealtimeClient then sends response.create while the user is speaking, resuming an interrupted old response.
findings.evidence: Local Node fake against dist/mcp.js (source hash matched requested source) produced followup:true for final event. Existing mcp.test.mjs:29-33 allocates call(a) and completes response.done before speech_started, so that test cannot detect this ordering.
findings.recommended_test: Add a lifecycle regression with response.created before speech_started but MCP progress/completion afterwards; assert no followup. Exercise same sequence through VoiceRealtimeClient and assert no response.create wire item. Also assert a genuinely new response.created after speech_started may follow up normally.
findings.recommended_fix: Allocate/track every response on response.created so barge-in invalidates responses even before their first MCP call; retain per-response cancellation when later events register calls.
regression_tests: packages/voice-core/tests/mcp.test.mjs: barge-in cancels a created response before its first delayed MCP call
packages/voice-core/tests/runtime.test.mjs: interruption before delayed first MCP call never sends an old followup
findings.resolution_evidence: Independent local sequence repeats original failing ordering against final dist/mcp.js: old response yields zero followups, newly created response yields exactly one, duplicate old/new completions yield zero additional followups. Committed regression includes actual VoiceRealtimeClient wire assertions for zero old response.create and exactly one new response.create.
findings.fix: Register responses on response.created so interruption before the first delayed MCP call cancels that old response permanently. New legitimate response still gets exactly one follow-up.

findings.problem: Replacing unified release_gate.py with job aggregation drops four prior mandatory guards: ci:text-integrity, ci:frontend-manifest, ci:legacy-guards, ci:runtime-integrity.
findings.reproduction: At prior reviewed source RUN_FRONTEND_GATES=1 invokes release_gate.py which invokes pnpm ci:gates, containing all four. At 98a no job command invokes ci:gates, release_gate.py or these four commands; static assertion finds all four absent. Other eight jobs can pass and synthetic PASS artifact is still written.
findings.consequence: Text corruption, frontend manifest drift, prohibited legacy implementation and runtime integrity failures can bypass the authoritative release checks. API unit tests are still covered by pnpm unit; this finding does not claim they were lost.
findings.resolution_evidence: Independently inspected actual workflow diff and executed actual workflow-derived condition/aggregate/environment scripts through regression suite. All relevant cases PASS.
findings.fix: Restore text integrity, frontend manifest, legacy guards and runtime integrity in authoritative CI Gates; propagate every required job failure.

findings.symbol: deploy-production job, first checkout, trust gate
findings.problem: Manual deploy checks out caller-supplied DEPLOY_SHA and executes that candidate check_release_review.py before establishing it is trusted/current-main/reviewed, with production secrets already in job environment.
findings.reproduction: Dispatch workflow from main with deploy_sha pointing to a non-main commit whose scripts/check_release_review.py contains arbitrary Python or simply exits zero. Initial checkout selects that commit; step79 executes its code before any trusted main/CI/review validation. Production environment restriction to main workflow ref does not bind input deploy_sha. No production action was performed during this static reproduction.
findings.consequence: Unreviewed candidate code executes with hotel SSH credentials, admin/provider/master secrets and GH token; it can bypass gate or access credentials before root transaction checking. The later root runtime fence remains intact but cannot undo runner credential exposure.
findings.resolution_evidence: Independently inspected actual workflow diff and executed actual workflow-derived condition/aggregate/environment scripts through regression suite. All relevant cases PASS.
findings.fix: Enforce trusted main workflow context and trusted checkout before release validation, candidate checkout and private production credential injection.

findings.problem: Cancellation job runs for manual/non-main diagnostics and defines stale as any different SHA. It can cancel newer authoritative current-main release runs.
findings.reproduction: Executed exact jq selector from pinned workflow using GITHUB_SHA=a*40/current run100 (manual diagnostic branch) and queued/in-progress CI Release push-main run200 at actual main b*40. Selector outputs200 for cancellation. Job has no push-main-only if condition and never reads actual current main or compares creation order.
findings.consequence: A legitimate manual diagnostic run can abort authoritative main validation and block/corrupt release provenance. A delayed/rerun older workflow can likewise target a newer different-SHA release.
findings.resolution_evidence: Independently inspected actual workflow diff and executed actual workflow-derived condition/aggregate/environment scripts through regression suite. All relevant cases PASS.
findings.fix: Delete unsafe cross-workflow cancellation and bind concurrency to source SHA; old/manual sources cannot cancel newer main source.
